summary:
**LunaPower 3D – Mission Aurora** is an interactive, browser-based 3D educational simulation game designed to demonstrate energy management in a lunar habitat. Players take the role of an astronaut responsible for maintaining the Moon Base's electricity supply for 72 simulated hours.

The game addresses the challenge of providing reliable energy for future lunar settlements, where limited battery storage, changing solar power availability, and equipment failures can threaten essential operations.

Players explore a moving 3D lunar environment, monitor solar generation, battery levels, and electricity demand, and interact with equipment such as solar panels, battery storage, and thermal control systems. They must respond to emergencies, including simulated solar dust storms, repair equipment, and manage optional electricity loads to prevent power shortages.

Developed using HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and Three.js, LunaPower 3D combines interactive gameplay with renewable energy education. The project is important because it makes complex energy-management concepts accessible, engaging, and easier to understand while highlighting the importance of sustainable power systems for future lunar exploration.

Project Details – LunaPower 3D: Mission Aurora

Team Name: LunarVolt
Challenge: Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer
Project: LunaPower 3D – Mission Aurora

Project Overview

LunaPower 3D – Mission Aurora is an interactive, browser-based 3D educational game developed by Team LunarVolt for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. Our project addresses the challenge "Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer" by creating a virtual lunar training environment where young aspiring astronauts can learn essential space mission concepts through exploration, decision-making, and interactive challenges.

Rather than relying only on traditional educational materials, our game allows learners to experience the responsibilities of managing a simulated lunar habitat.

How Does Our Project Work?

Players take the role of an astronaut exploring a three-dimensional Moon Base. Using keyboard controls, they can move around the environment, locate equipment, and interact with different systems, including solar panels, battery storage, thermal control equipment, communication systems, and research facilities.

The main objective is to maintain the habitat's electricity supply for 72 simulated hours.

Throughout the mission, players monitor solar power generation, battery levels, electricity demand, and mission progress using an interactive dashboard.

The game introduces simulated emergency scenarios, including reduced solar generation, low battery levels, and equipment malfunctions. Players must respond by repairing equipment, managing electricity consumption, and prioritizing essential systems.

Successful actions contribute to the mission score, while poor energy-management decisions can result in mission failure.

A guided tutorial helps new players understand the controls and mission objectives before attempting the complete challenge.

Benefits and Educational Value

Our game introduces junior astronauts to several important concepts:

  • Renewable energy and solar electricity generation
  • Battery energy storage and resource conservation
  • Energy supply and demand management
  • Basic lunar habitat operations
  • Emergency response and problem-solving
  • Critical thinking and decision-making
  • Understanding the consequences of operational choices

By learning through gameplay, students can explore technical concepts in an accessible and engaging environment.

Intended Impact

The primary goal of LunaPower 3D is to inspire young learners to become interested in space exploration, engineering, renewable energy, and STEM education.

The project demonstrates how interactive simulations can help students develop practical reasoning skills and understand the importance of managing limited resources during space missions.

As a browser-based educational tool, the game can potentially support classroom demonstrations, introductory STEM activities, and independent learning without requiring specialized gaming hardware.

Technologies and Tools Used

We developed the game using:

  • HTML5: To structure the game interface and menus.
  • CSS3: To design the dashboard, mission alerts, and visual elements.
  • JavaScript: To implement game mechanics, energy-management calculations, equipment interactions, scoring, and mission progression.
  • Three.js: To create and render the interactive 3D lunar environment.
  • WebGL: To support real-time 3D graphics in the browser.
  • Web Audio API: To provide background audio and interactive sound effects.

The prototype runs in a modern desktop web browser and uses keyboard-based controls.

Creativity and Innovation

The creative aspect of LunaPower 3D is its combination of astronaut exploration with interactive energy-management training.

Instead of simply presenting information about lunar missions, the game places learners in situations where their decisions directly affect mission outcomes.

Its key features include:

  • An explorable 3D lunar habitat
  • Astronaut-controlled equipment interactions
  • Simulated energy generation and consumption
  • Battery management and load prioritization
  • Emergency scenarios with visual warnings
  • Interactive mission objectives and scoring
  • Guided training and mission success or failure feedback

This approach transforms technical learning into a mission-based experience that encourages exploration and experimentation.

Important Design Considerations

During development, our team focused on educational accessibility, ease of use, interactive learning, and clear mission objectives.

We designed the experience around simplified energy-management principles so that younger learners can understand the relationship between electricity generation, storage, and consumption.

We also considered the importance of immediate feedback, intuitive controls, visually identifiable equipment, and progressively introduced challenges.

The game is an educational simulation rather than a scientifically validated astronaut training system. Its energy values and emergency scenarios are simplified for learning purposes.

Conclusion

LunaPower 3D – Mission Aurora demonstrates how interactive gaming can make astronaut training concepts more engaging and accessible to young learners.

By combining lunar exploration, renewable energy management, emergency response, and problem-solving, our project supports the goals of the "Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer" challenge.

Our vision is to encourage the next generation of astronauts, scientists, and engineers to explore space-related challenges through creativity, curiosity, and hands-on learning.

Explore the Moon. Manage the Energy. Save the Mission.
